correctness.rationale: For every fixed \(k\ge3\) and its \(2^{\binom{k}{2}}\) labelled patterns, derive the exact radial-tangent factorization with \(d-1\)-dimensional tangent sphere and Gram determinant exponent \((d-k-2)/2\). Expanding log det gives a cubic triangle term with coefficient \(1/\sqrt d\); the integral of each centered triangle monomial is zero and the integrated remainder is \(o(d^{-1/2})\). In the critical cap \(h=\lambda d^{-1/4}\), radial overshoots converge with moments to rate-one exponentials, and threshold perturbations contribute \(2+\lambda^4\); for \(h=a/\sqrt d\), the truncated Gaussian radial moment contributes \(\mu_a^2\). Integrating against smooth Gaussian half-spaces yields all edge and triangle coefficients. The proof distinguishes exact scales and boundaries and applies only for fixed k. Direct finite simulation and coefficient normalization in check_cap_graph.py passed; this does not prove the infinite statement.

value.rationale: The radius \(d^{-1/4}\) is a geometric signal/noise threshold for nonobtuse pair incidence among independently cap-uniform directions. The all-labelled-pattern expansion separates edge bias from irreducible three-vertex geometric dependence and shows a noncommuting \(d^{-1/2}\) equatorial cap boundary layer. These quantify clustering in spherical sampling beyond a routine limit statement and provide a calibration for fixed-size motif statistics.
